engagement_title: Vanguard Motors forecourt changeover: pull a bright-overcast lot shoot to one house look, recover the dealership shield off a weathered forecourt plate, rebuild the printer's window card into a live run, and hand the forecourt and the sales floor one editable set
vertical: Automotive, Industrial and Agriculture, independent prestige used-vehicle dealership selling to retail buyers and part-exchange customers (Harrogate, North Yorkshire)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring dealership brief posted on Upwork and Freelancer.com, 'window cards / forecourt spec cards for our stock, one per vehicle, from our stock feed', where the dealer supplies a spreadsheet exported from the stock management system carrying registration, stock number, price, mileage and a spec block, plus a folder of photographs taken on the lot, and asks for a printed card per car so the forecourt stops looking like a collection of handwritten prices. Co-anchor: the equally common 'we only have the PDF our printer made' brief, where the working file is gone and the client's standing instruction is to keep the card exactly as it is and put this month's stock through it, with named single-vehicle files needed because a card is reprinted the day a car sells. The ledger records this slot (LAYOUT-B-14) as a record-per-page merge with a per-vehicle photo column, one_line_ask 'so every car on the lot displays a consistent branded card', and the triage verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept, the collateral set and the price-band logic are right, but as banked the engagement sat almost entirely on the merge surface with the lot photography and the dealership's own mark treated as plumbing. LAYOUT-32 keeps the concept and the deliverables and restores the commission the dealer actually posts: the photography has to be fixed because it was shot in one bright overcast morning, the shield has to be recovered because the only clean version left is the plate above the office door, and the point of fixing both is that the window cards, the forecourt board and the Monday sales meeting all come out of one stock list and have to agree. All vehicle marques and models named in the engagement are coined; no real manufacturer, dealer group, finance house or regulator appears.
client_one_liner: Fourteen cars on the forecourt, a morning's photography where half the panels are blown out, a window card the printer built and we cannot open, and a stock feed that still lists cars we sold last week.
client_brief:
Vanguard Motors, forecourt changeover.

We are an independent dealer. We hold about fourteen cars at a time, we buy carefully and we sell to people who have already decided roughly what they want and are deciding where to buy it. Every car on the forecourt carries a card inside the windscreen: what it is, the year, the mileage, the specification that matters and the price. Right now half of those cards are last month's and two are handwritten, and that is what a buyer sees before anyone walks out to meet them.

The photography is the first problem. We photographed the whole lot on one bright overcast morning and finished the last few late in the afternoon when the light had gone. Laid out together they do not look like one forecourt. The silver and white cars are the awkward ones: on the screen the bonnets and the roofs have gone to nothing and the sky behind them is a flat white. The paint colour matters more than anything else on the card, because a buyer who drives forty miles for a car in one colour and finds another one on the forecourt does not buy it.

What we need from the pictures: every car looking like it was photographed the same morning, the colour honest, and one picture per car that sits in the card's window without cutting the front of the vehicle off.

There is also our shield. It is on the cards, on the board at the entrance and on the sold slips. The artwork is long gone, so what we have is a photograph of the pressed plate above the office door.

The second problem is the cards. Our printer produced our window cards two seasons ago off our old system. We have the file they sent and nothing else, and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it as it is and put the current stock, specs and prices through it. Send us the press file, and send us one card per car named to the stock number, because when a car sells at four on a Friday somebody has to find that one card and reprint it.

Then the pieces we do not have. A panel for the entrance board, a counter sheet of this month's finance offers, and a short set of slides for the Monday sales meeting. All of that back as one file we can edit ourselves, because prices move every week.

Cars run eighteen to ninety-five thousand pounds and the buyer is thirty-five to sixty. Photograph forward, quiet, no shouting. Our feed is attached, and if anything in it looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Vehicles from 18,000 pounds (a low-mileage compact estate, a four-year-old hatchback) to 95,000 pounds (a two-year-old grand tourer, a specification-heavy performance saloon). Buyer 35 to 60, a private retail buyer who has already narrowed the choice online, has driven a distance to see one specific car, and is deciding whether this dealer is careful. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short specification of the things that differ between examples, the price present and plainly set rather than shouted, the finance line legible and secondary, and generous space. Push it toward the budget lot register, the monthly payment set enormous, a burst badge, a saturated red price flash, three exclamation points of specification, and a 95,000 pound car reads as a car with something wrong with it, which is the exact commercial failure this dealer is paying to avoid. Push it the other way into a manufacturer-style brochure with no price and no mileage and the card stops doing the one job it has, which is answering the two questions a buyer has while standing in the rain. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 pounds fixed, or 45 to 70 pounds an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.sector: An independent prestige used vehicle dealership selling to retail buyers and part exchange customers from a single forecourt.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2006, one forecourt in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. A small independent holding about fourteen cars at a time, buying selectively rather than to volume.
brand_identity.about: Vanguard holds around fourteen carefully bought cars at a time and sells to people who have already decided roughly what they want and are choosing where to buy it. The card in the windscreen is the first thing a buyer meets, before anyone walks out, so it has to answer their two questions honestly: what is this car, and what does it cost.
brand_identity.audience: Private retail buyers aged 35 to 60 who have narrowed the choice online, driven a distance to see one specific car, and are deciding whether this dealer is careful.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent prestige used. Cars from 18,000 pounds to 95,000. Photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short spec of what differs between examples, the price plainly set and the finance line legible but secondary. Never the budget lot register, never a manufacturer brochure with no price.
brand_identity.typography: A confident low contrast serif or sturdy grotesque for the marque and headline, paired with a clean neutral sans for the spec block, price and finance footer. Careful and quiet, neither discount loud nor brochure sparse.
brand_identity.voice: Factual, unhurried and confident, a dealer who lets the car and the spec do the talking. No exclamation, no urgency. Example: One owner, full history, the colour it says on the card and the colour it is on the forecourt.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The shield artwork is long gone. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door, weathered by several winters, carrying the shield at about 180mm. The current stock, specs and prices arrive from the stock feed, and the finance wording is fixed by the broker.
brand_identity.values: Cars bought with care and sold without spin, and a forecourt where the card and the vehicle always agree.

assets_supplied.name: lot_photos/ (18 frames, 5200 x 3400)
assets_supplied.kind: The dealer's own photography of fourteen vehicles taken on the forecourt across one bright overcast morning and one late afternoon, handheld, with a few alternate wider frames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole lot in one morning, the last few late on. The silver and white ones have gone to nothing on the screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The white and silver cars' bonnets and roofs and the sky behind them are genuinely clipped rather than merely bright, so a highlight recovery on those frames returns an image visually identical to the one that went in while reporting complete success, and no response says the data was not there. Separately, three vehicles were shot so tight that the card's landscape window cannot be taken from them without cutting the front wing, and the crop tool responds by offering an expand chain that would fabricate bodywork on a car a buyer will stand in front of.

assets_supplied.name: windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the current window card, A4 portrait, one vehicle per page, fonts embedded, produced from the dealer's old system through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries the shield, a vehicle photograph, a headline, a two-column spec block, the price and the finance footer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us two seasons ago. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The conversion returns nothing like the structure the printed page suggests. The tidy two-column spec block, the price line and the finance footer all arrive as ONE continuous tab-delimited story that has to be driven by ordered offsets, while the single-looking headline splits into three separate frames because year, marque and model were placed as separate runs, and the two graphic frames (the vehicle photograph and the shield) are distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, neither being named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: stock_feed.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the dealership's stock management system, one row per unit, with columns for stock number, registration, marque, model, derivative, year, mileage, colour, transmission, fuel, a nine-item spec block, price, monthly figure, status and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the system on Monday morning. The prices are what we are asking today."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Seventeen rows for fourteen cars actually on the forecourt: three sold or reserved units the system still emits, flagged only by a status column the dealer never mentions. Stock numbers have lost their leading zeros to the spreadsheet that exported them, one car's mileage cell is empty, two derivative names run four times the length of the rest because the clerk pasted the full factory description, prices sit as raw integers with no separators or currency, and the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds one car's photograph to every card or binds none at all.

assets_supplied.name: forecourt_plate.jpg (3800 x 2600)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door carrying the Vanguard Motors shield at about 180mm wide, weathered by several winters, shot in flat daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of the shield we have. The artwork went years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The shield is a bordered device with an enclosed chevron counter and a hairline keyline inside the outer edge, and the plate's weathering means the trace comes back carrying near-identical greys as separate fills and slightly broken edges along that keyline. It reads perfectly at inspection scale and on white, and the card reproduces it at roughly a fifth of the plate's size on a deep midnight ground.

assets_supplied.name: finance_wording.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The wording the dealership's finance broker requires on any printed material carrying a monthly figure, 310 characters, supplied as plain text.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This has to appear on every card that shows a monthly payment, word for word, and it is not ours to change."

assets_supplied.name: forecourt_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of the forecourt and the entrance board, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the forecourt. The board is by the gate."

acceptance_bar: All fourteen cars read as one forecourt: one white point, one black point, one vehicle scale in the card window, judged with the fourteen laid out together rather than one at a time.
Paint colour is honest on every car, and no correction has moved a silver toward blue, a white toward cream or a black into crush. A colour a buyer would dispute on arrival is a rejected picture.
No bodywork, badge, wheel or panel edge anywhere in the delivered set has been invented, extended or reconstructed by any tool.
Every card window shows the vehicle without cutting the front or rear of it, at a consistent scale across the set.
No delivered file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

The recovered shield is delivered as placeable artwork with the chevron counter genuinely open, no opaque backing box, and it must still read as the shield at the size it is actually reproduced on the card, on the card's own ground, not only at the size it was inspected.

Window cards: exactly one page per vehicle actually on the forecourt, every field the current card carries present on every page, every value bound verbatim from the feed, and the photograph on each card the car named on that card.
The finance wording appears in full and word for word on every card that shows a monthly figure. If it does not fit the card as it stands, tell us in writing before it prints rather than trimming it.
Nothing in the feed may be shortened, reworded or abbreviated to make it fit, and no card may go out carrying a specification line that stops mid word.

The press file renders at real print resolution at A4 trim, and there is one single-vehicle file per car named to its stock number, containing the car its name claims, verified by opening it rather than by the order it came back in.
The entrance board panel, the finance counter sheet and the Monday slides come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from.
In that file the words are live text, the finance offers are a real table and the shield is real artwork, not a picture of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
A written note: what was done to each picture and why it differs from its neighbours, anything in our feed you questioned and what you did about it, and anything the card could not carry.

Derives the card window crop and the wider lot crop per vehicle without inventing bodywork, which rules out the expand chain the crop tool offers on the three tight frames. Counted honestly as one surface: image_vectorize is a Photoshop-family tool and no Illustrator tool is called anywhere in this engagement.

The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair, and it has to read as a careful independent dealer rather than as a discount lot or as a manufacturer brochure. The handover must also state that no face chosen here can reach the printed window card, since there is no font file download, so the card's typography stays the printer's.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, isGenTech excluded, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board

Plus the persistent board the sales manager approves the stock set from before the press file is committed, sent within the twelve-item placement cap and reconciled against failedItems.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The window cards are record per page against a layout the dealer has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The board panel, finance sheet and slides do not exist yet, need three canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Authoring the cards from scratch throws away the card the printer built; trying to merge the board panel discovers record per page cannot produce three canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eighteen lot frames, the window card PDF, the stock feed, the plate photograph and the finance wording, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline: forty artefacts later the mapping between URL and stock number has to still be trustworthy, and stock number is the thing every deliverable is keyed to.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by stock number and role.

trajectory.action: Preview every frame and triage: which session, how exposed, how level, how tightly framed, what colour the car actually is, and whether the frames and the feed describe the same fourteen cars.
trajectory.judgement: The dealer says one morning. The last few disagree. The agent also has to notice which frames are framed too tight to yield the card window before it plans any crop, and to read a seventeen-row feed against fourteen cars on a forecourt.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering session, exposure, level, framing headroom and identity against the feed.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, which matters most on exactly the frames that already have no headroom, so it precedes every crop decision.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one house white from the morning session, correct each vehicle toward it with its own parameter set, and attempt to bring back the bonnets, roofs and sky on the frames the dealer flagged as gone.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across fourteen frames, not fourteen locally optimised pictures. The afternoon frames need a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral, and recovery has to be judged by looking at the result rather than by the call returning.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log and the result of every recovery attempt recorded.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections to protect the paint: hold silver off blue, keep white from going cream, keep black panels from crushing shut, and keep glass and tyres from dragging the whole frame.
trajectory.judgement: Paint colour is the dealer's commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one. Prompt wording is the gate, and a selection named for the car pulls the glass and the shadow under it with it, which has to be recognised as the wrong selection rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Paint-protected masters with masked parameters recorded per stock number.

trajectory.action: Derive the card window crop and the wider lot crop per vehicle, reading the detection confidence and tradeoffs each crop returns, and deal with the frames that cannot yield the window without cutting the car.
trajectory.judgement: The crop tool will offer to expand the frame, and on a car that a buyer will walk up to, fabricated bodywork is a false claim about the vehicle rather than a convenience. The alternative is a different frame, a different crop policy or an honest escalation, and the choice has to be made and disclosed.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen card windows and fourteen lot crops at a settled vehicle scale, with the crop metadata transcribed and every expand offer refused in writing.

trajectory.action: Propose two treatments for the card photograph, the car left in its forecourt context and the car lifted onto a single graded ground, and pick one against a prestige used buyer and against the card's own dark ground.
trajectory.judgement: A taste decision with a defence attached and a downstream dependency: a lifted car has to sit on a ground that works with the printer's card, and the wrong choice is only fixable by reprocessing all fourteen.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed treatments and a written pick with the reason recorded.

trajectory.action: Produce the card photograph per vehicle to the chosen treatment, routing per car rather than applying one policy to fourteen.
trajectory.judgement: A dark car against a wet dark tarmac and a white car against a bright sky do not lift the same way, and a knockout that succeeds is not the same as an edge that follows the bodywork.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen card photographs with the route recorded per stock number.

trajectory.action: Recover the shield from the forecourt plate: select the painted device by its own visual properties rather than by the plate it sits on, invert, crop to the selection's own bounds, trace it, strip the trace's full-canvas backing path and inject a viewBox, then consolidate the weathering into the artwork it is meant to be.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the plate pulls the aluminium and the trace returns a rectangle. The enclosed chevron counter cannot be punched by a knockout, so the route is selection and fill, and a trace carrying forty near-identical greys is output rather than artwork.
trajectory.produces: The shield as placeable vector with no backing box, plus a raster plate of the same artwork for the printed card.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the stock feed against the pictures and the forecourt, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, restore the stock numbers, settle price and mileage formatting, upload the card photographs and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real data-prep work: units already sold, stock numbers mangled by a spreadsheet, an empty mileage cell, prices with no formatting and an image column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which are the dealer's, and how to say so before anything prints.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded photographs, the image map, and a first list of questions for the dealer.

trajectory.action: Convert the window card to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the dealer's old system happened to produce, not by what the printed card looks like. Two graphic frames come back distinguishable only by bounds and link, and deciding which one holds the vehicle photograph is a judgement made against the printed reference rather than a name in the response.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real integer ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping across the separate headline frames and the single body story plus the photograph, ordering any rows that share a uid in descending position against the original text, and pass it back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Two different mapping strategies inside one card, one per frame and one by ordered offsets, chosen by what the document actually is. Every offset computed from a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and the whole mapping passed across as one stringified object with integer page-item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the headline frames, the body story and the image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create, and render a single record to settle which graphic frame received the photograph.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and settling frame identity by looking at a rendered page against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory and image binding have been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with each car's own photograph bound and the sold and reserved units excluded by record range, render the press file and 300 ppi proofs, and produce one single-vehicle file per car named to its stock number, identity-verified by opening each file.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution and returns multi-record output in an order that does not match the feed, so both the resolution route and the per-record route are chosen deliberately. Naming fourteen cards by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a salesperson discovers in a windscreen.
trajectory.produces: The press card file at A4, 300 ppi proofs, and fourteen identity-verified files named to stock number.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card at true trim against the feed and against the printed reference, field by field, photograph by photograph and shield by shield.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a spec line that stops early, a photograph in the shield's frame and a mark that has closed up all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible on a screen-scale proof.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation of the rendered window cards against the feed.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one road or landscape frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, grade it toward the house neutral and judge it beside the lot set. Then build the approval board within the placement cap and re-send only the entries reported as failed.
trajectory.judgement: An atmosphere frame at this band has to read as a plausible drive rather than as a dusk supercar advertisement, which is the wrong register for a careful independent dealer and reads as a car with something wrong with it.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded and judged in or out, and a persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read careful and quiet rather than either discount or manufacturer. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the entire kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with roots at three canvas sizes (A1 entrance board panel at true physical dimensions, A4 finance counter sheet, Monday slides), the finance offers as a real table, the recovered shield as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas size. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and the remaining canvases through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. The design decisions, how much of the A1 is car and how much is offer, whether the counter sheet leads with the monthly figure or the car, are the actual work and they are where the price band is either honoured or lost.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document at three canvas sizes, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to let the next freelancer rebuild the card from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name the units excluded, the frames that could not yield the window honestly, and anything the card could not carry, before a printer sees the file.
trajectory.produces: The written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether there is anything left to recover in the blown areas. The dealer describes the bonnets and roofs of the white and silver cars as gone, which reads as an exposure complaint, and the natural response is a highlight recovery pass. On these particular frames the readout is that nothing moves: the call succeeds, returns an image, and the recovered file is visually indistinguishable from the one that went in, because those pixels are genuinely clipped rather than merely bright. Nothing in any response says so. Which frames are recoverable and which are not is a property of these exposures and cannot be known from the dealer's description, from the previews (a bright roof and a clipped roof look the same on screen) or from the session split, because two afternoon frames recover fully and three morning frames do not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn whether the data survived is to attempt the recovery and compare the result against the input, and the tool reports success in both cases. Nothing states it: the brief says the panels have gone to nothing, which is a client describing a symptom, and no asset description names which vehicles are unrecoverable. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change what the picture is rather than to redo the correction, which reopens the crop policy and the treatment decision for the affected cars.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each recovery result against its input rather than accepting the call, then handle the unrecoverable frames a different way: re-frame from an alternate wider frame where one exists so less clipped sky is carried, re-decide the card window crop so the blown roof sits outside it, or, where neither works, escalate that the car needs rephotographing rather than shipping a card with a hole in the bodywork. Then re-judge white point and vehicle scale across all fourteen, because cars re-framed for a different reason will not sit with the rest unless the policy is re-taken as a set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A forecourt of cards on which the most expensive white and silver cars have a featureless white hole where the bonnet and roof should be, printed and put in the windscreens of the actual vehicles, by a dealer whose entire pitch is that he is careful.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows a tidy two-column spec block, one price line, one footer, one headline and one photograph, and every sensible plan maps those as separate frames. The conversion returns the opposite shape: the spec block, the price and the finance footer arrive as one continuous tab-delimited story that can only be driven by ordered offsets, while the single-looking headline splits into three separate frames because year, marque and model were placed as separate runs, and the two graphic frames carry no name, only bounds and a link, so which one holds the vehicle photograph and which holds the shield is not stated anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity from a PDF is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export IDML and read, and the shape it returns is the inverse of the one the printed page implies. Nothing states it: the brief says only to keep the card as it is and put the current stock through it, and names no frames, stories or fields. It is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy itself changes, from per-field frames to two different strategies inside one card, and the image binding has to be settled by rendering a page rather than by reading the response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the planned per-field map. Reconstruct the true story from the IDML content runs, compute offsets against that string for everything in the body, map the three headline frames individually by their integer page-item ids, and settle the photograph's frame by rendering one record and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph. Then rebuild, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify the placeholders before any card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A template that validates and reports success while binding the model into the year's frame and the vehicle photograph into the shield's frame, producing fourteen cards that are confidently wrong in the two places a buyer looks first.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered shield survives its own reproduction. Traced off a 180mm pressed plate it is immaculate at inspection scale and on a white ground, and it carries perfectly onto the A1 entrance panel. The window card reproduces it at roughly a fifth of that size on the card's deep midnight ground, and at that size on that ground the hairline keyline and the enclosed chevron counter fill in and the shield reads as a solid lozenge, while the plate's weathering, which was invisible as texture, shows as broken edges. This cannot be judged from the trace, from the SVG on screen or from the A1, because it is a product of the reproduction size, the ink behaviour of the card's dark ground and the specific edge quality this particular trace inherited from a weathered plate.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the artwork is genuinely correct at every size it is inspected at until it is rendered at true trim on the real ground, and no tool reports a reproduction limit. Nothing states it: the brief says the shield is on the cards and the board, and never asks how small it can go, so nothing has already discovered it. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to author a different piece of artwork for the small dark application rather than to re-place the same one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Produce a reproduction cut of the shield for the card: reduce the trace to the marks that survive at card size, open or drop the hairline keyline, keep the chevron counter open, and consolidate the weathering greys into flat fills, then re-generate the raster plate the merge binds, re-merge and re-render, and check it again at true trim on the dark ground rather than on screen. Keep the full-detail artwork for the A1 panel and record in the handover which version belongs where and below what size the detailed one stops holding.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen window cards and every sold slip carrying a shield that has closed into an unreadable dark blob, on the one element that appears on every printed thing this dealership owns, delivered as a recovered brand asset.

deliverables.name: Vanguard forecourt photography, fourteen vehicles at one house look
deliverables.spec: Eighteen supplied frames reconciled to fourteen vehicles and brought to one house white and one black point across two lighting sessions, paint colour honest on every car, delivered as one card window and one wider lot picture per vehicle at a consistent vehicle scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. No bodywork invented anywhere. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, the outcome of every highlight recovery attempt recorded, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Card-ready vehicle photographs to the agreed treatment
deliverables.spec: Fourteen vehicles prepared to the single agreed card treatment, with the edge following the bodywork rather than the tarmac or the sky, no halo carried in from a bright ground, and the route recorded per stock number because a dark car on wet tarmac and a white car against a blown sky cannot be produced the same way. Judged at card reproduction size on the card's own dark ground rather than on the original.

deliverables.name: The Vanguard shield, recovered as placeable artwork
deliverables.spec: The dealership shield recovered from a photograph of a weathered pressed plate and delivered as placeable vector with the chevron counter genuinely open, no opaque backing box, a real viewBox so it scales, and consolidated flat fills rather than the plate's weathering as separate greys. Delivered in the two forms the job actually needs, a full-detail cut for large application and a reproduction cut that holds at window-card size on a dark ground, with a note stating which belongs where and below what size the detailed one fails.

deliverables.name: Forecourt window card run, press file plus per-stock-number files
deliverables.spec: A4 portrait, one vehicle per page in feed order, page count equal to the count of cars actually on the forecourt with sold and reserved units excluded by record range, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every card binds year, marque, model, derivative, mileage, colour, the nine-item spec block, price and the finance wording verbatim from the feed, plus that car's own photograph in the correct graphic frame. Accompanied by one single-vehicle file per car named to its stock number and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Entrance board panel, finance counter sheet and Monday slides
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document holding roots at three canvas sizes: an A1 entrance board panel at true physical dimensions, an A4 finance offers counter sheet, and the Monday sales-meeting slides. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, the finance offers as a genuine table, the recovered shield as real vector artwork, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, so weekly price changes need no re-commission and the design survives the document's own retention.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, which frames could not be recovered and what was done instead, every expand offer refused and why, how the shield was recovered and which cut belongs at which size, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the explicit statement that the card's typography remains the printer's because no font can reach that surface, what the conversion exposed and the two mapping strategies taken against it, every feed row questioned and its resolution, anything the card could not carry, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the graded stock set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press card file has exactly one page per vehicle actually on the forecourt in feed order and renders at 300 ppi at A4 trim, with no page for a sold or reserved unit.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the rendered file against the reconciled forecourt count, check the render call's resolution and the output raster dimensions, and read the stock number off every page against the excluded rows.

verifiers_auto.text: Every field the current card carries, including the full finance wording, appears on every merged page and matches its feed row verbatim, with no line ending mid word.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip the prepared template to IDML and grep for every expected placeholder, then read text off each rendered page at true trim and compare against its source row character for character.

verifiers_auto.text: Fourteen single-vehicle files exist, each named to a stock number, each containing the car its name claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the stock number and registration off each single-page file and compare with its filename, never with its position in the returned list.

verifiers_auto.text: Each card carries the photograph of the car named on that card, in the photograph's frame rather than the shield's.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the headline off each rendered page and compare with the bound photograph and with the printed reference card's frame positions.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered picture contains invented pixels: no generative expand output appears anywhere in the delivered set, and every crop or resize response is free of an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect every imaging response for expand calls and for tradeoffs entries, and compare every delivered dimension against its source dimension.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported Express document holds three canvases at three distinct declared sizes with the entrance panel at true A1 physical dimensions, every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, the shield present as path shapes, and the finance offers present as real table cells.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide dimensions from the export response and parse each canvas's returned markup for placeholder images, path-type shapes, table cell structure and resolved positions running past the declared canvas width.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported document carries a resolved licensed face and the intended numeric weight rather than a silent fallback.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the resolved font families and weights in the returned markup against the kit's families and the numeric weights read from the style inventory.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out together, the fourteen cars read as one forecourt photographed on one morning at one vehicle scale.
verifiers_human.how: View the fourteen card windows together and judge white point, black point and vehicle scale as a set rather than one at a time.

verifiers_human.text: Paint colour is honest on every car, with no silver pushed blue, no white pushed cream and no black crushed shut.
verifiers_human.how: Compare each delivered picture against its source frame and against the colour named in the feed row, at the size the card reproduces it.

verifiers_human.text: No card window cuts the front or rear of the vehicle, and no bodywork anywhere has been invented.
verifiers_human.how: Compare each card window against its source frame and check the handover for the frames that could not yield the window and what was done instead.

verifiers_human.text: The shield still reads as the shield at the size it is printed on the card, on the card's own dark ground.
verifiers_human.how: View the rendered card at true trim and check the chevron counter and the keyline are still open and legible, then compare against the shield on the A1 panel.

verifiers_human.text: The collateral reads photograph forward and quiet, appropriate to an 18,000 to 95,000 pound car and a buyer who has already narrowed the choice, rather than budget-lot loud or manufacturer-brochure silent.
verifiers_human.how: Review the cards, the entrance panel, the finance sheet and the slides against the price band and audience description and reject enormous monthly figures, burst badges and saturated price flashes, as well as layouts that omit price or mileage.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals, naming the excluded units, the unrecoverable frames, the refused expands and the fact that the card's typography could not be changed.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage, conversion and render findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: window cards to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, forecourt set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which session sets the house white, knowing a late-afternoon reference makes every silver car on the lot look warm.
Whether a highlight recovery actually recovered anything, on frames where the response looks the same either way.

What to do with a car whose card window cannot be taken without cutting it: a different frame, a different crop policy, or an honest escalation, given that the expand chain would fabricate bodywork on a car the buyer will stand in front of.
Whether the card photograph is the car in its forecourt context or the car lifted onto a graded ground, decided against the printer's own dark card rather than against the screen.
Vehicle scale across the set, decided as a forecourt rather than per car, and re-decided once any car is re-framed for a different reason.
How to name the selection that recovers the shield: naming the plate pulls the aluminium, naming the painted device's own colour and form pulls the mark.

Whether the traced shield is artwork or merely output, including the backing path that rides along, the weathering carried as separate fills, and whether one cut can serve both an A1 panel and a small dark card.
Which of two unnamed graphic frames holds the vehicle photograph rather than the shield.
Whether to map per frame or by ordered offsets, when one card requires both strategies at once.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
How to honour 'nothing shortened or reworded' when a pasted factory derivative or the finance wording does not fit the frame the printer built.
Whether the sold and reserved units are the agent's call to exclude or the dealer's, and how that is disclosed before printing.
Whether to name fourteen single-vehicle files by the order they came back or by opening each one.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a careful independent dealer, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed card at all.
Whether the licensed frame reads as a plausible drive or as a dusk supercar advertisement, which is the wrong register for this band.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this folder into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of cars. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific vehicles, each with a registration, a stock number, a mileage and a paint colour that a buyer has driven forty miles to see, and a generated car fabricates a wheel, a badge, a trim level or a colour, which on a card that also carries a price is a false claim about the goods. The dealership shield is a specific pressed device that must come back as the same shield, because it is already on the board at the gate. SPEC: the dealer needs one card per car actually on the forecourt at A4 and 300 ppi with every value bound verbatim from their own stock feed, sold and reserved units absent, the full finance wording present word for word, each card carrying its own photograph, and one separately named file per stock number containing the car its filename claims. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next week's stock is a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move every week. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did anything survive in that blown roof, did this placeholder get created, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, does this shield still read at card size. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), the surface count is five and honestly declared, and no Illustrator tool is claimed: image_vectorize is counted as Photoshop-family, and document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector are never called because they sit on a polling helper this host does not have. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified; one record per page is confirmed for PDF output so page count equals forecourt count is an exact gate; recordRange subsetting is verified and is how sold and reserved units are excluded; outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored, so 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout on the merged .indd using the N-N pageRange form. PER-VEHICLE FILES ARE PRODUCED BY AN ORDER-VERIFIED ROUTE: merge to application/x-indesign then document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles, or a recordRange loop, both verified in correct order, and multi-record raster output is never used for identity because v3 records its URLs coming back reversed with lying labels. Per-row image binding through an at-prefixed column with bare filenames plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually, and PDF-derived templates are confirmed to expose real graphic frames with imageHref and bounds. THE GRANULARITY CHECKPOINT IS A DOCUMENTED LIVE FINDING: v3 records that frame granularity from a PDF is not under the agent's control, that a continuous flow collapses to one text frame while placed images split the flow into multiple text frames plus graphic frames, and that you cannot spec a per-field frame map without exporting IDML and looking, which is exactly the inversion this card is built to produce. The source PDF is specified as a real font-embedding press PDF because thin synthetic PDFs fail conversion opaquely. IMAGING: auto_straighten, auto_tone, highlight and light-portion adjustments, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, colour temperature, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array and its requires_expand_chain offer, remove_background with backgroundColor, fill_area and vectorize are all verified headless; the substrate-versus-device prompt asymmetry, the enclosed-counter failure of remove_background, the binary mask, the opaque path-0 rect and the missing viewBox are documented findings. The clipped-highlight checkpoint rests on the fact that no imaging tool reports any measurement at all (no eyedropper, no histogram, no readout), so a recovery that moves nothing is indistinguishable from one that worked except by looking at the two images. Generative expand exists and is deliberately refused rather than used, which is the scored decision; no upscaling is asserted, since crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 and A4 are true physical canvases, tables survive as real tables, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport goes through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end, with the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call all in play, and the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface stated to the client. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, never the broken orientation filter, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no object removal, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
